answer: The admission burn is multiplied by 18 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival burns the most. The anchor multiplier is published, charged in basalt, and dune lists each payment. A burst of registrations hence prices itself out, as the marginal alias burns more than the first by design. A farm of 804 identities would post 798 proofs and burn roughly 89 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
